S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

symptom.disease_info: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) is characterized by recurrent, intrusive thoughts, images, or urges (obsessions) and/or repetitive behaviors or mental acts (compulsions) that the person feels driven to perform. These symptoms are time-consuming or cause significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. The course is often chronic with waxing and waning severity, frequently exacerbated by stress, increased responsibility, or role transitions. OCD is distinguished from generalized anxiety and other disorders by the presence of specific, stereotyped obsessions and compulsions that are recognized as excessive or unreasonable at some point and are not solely attributable to psychotic processes or the direct effects of substances or medical conditions.

patient.stressor: Hector had always been a meticulous planner, using spreadsheets to manage projects, travel, and even his vinyl collection, but he generally balanced this with salsa dancing, community events, and pickup basketball. When his company underwent a major reorganization two years ago, he was promoted to oversee a larger IT infrastructure portfolio, including cybersecurity for several high-profile clients, which dramatically increased his sense of responsibility and the potential consequences of mistakes. Over the following months, he started staying later and later at the office and at home, repeatedly reviewing configurations and incident reports, and turning down salsa socials and tech meetups he used to enjoy because he felt compelled to keep checking and rechecking his work. The tipping point came when he missed a critical family celebration and then had a minor panic episode on the train home after realizing that, despite all his late nights, he still felt unable to trust that things were "safe"; a colleague who noticed his deteriorating sleep and performance urged him to see a psychiatrist, and Hector finally agreed when he recognized that his checking routines had become unmanageable and were crowding out nearly everything else in his life.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m stuck in this loop of double- and triple-checking my work for hours, and I can’t move on even when I know it’s already done right.”

S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.
S065.manifestation: Lately my brain keeps ambushing me with these vivid flashes of a server getting hacked because I missed one tiny setting, or my nephew getting hurt because I didn’t check a door lock, and even when I tell myself it’s irrational and I’ve already verified everything, the “what if you missed something” loop just won’t shut off and drowns out whatever else I’m trying to do.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: When I finish a security change or even just lock my front door, I feel this crushing need to go back and reread every line of the config or jiggle the handle over and over, sometimes for an hour or more, because until I repeat the whole ritual just right I can’t shake the feeling that if I stop, something catastrophic will happen and it’ll be my fault.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: My checking has gotten so out of hand that I miss family events, avoid social things I used to love, and even at work my productivity has dropped because I burn hours re-reviewing tasks instead of moving projects forward.
